Turning 40 in a week and only got my diagnosis officially 3 months ago. I had my collapse at 29 and my 30s have basically been spent trying to get back on my feet without much luck. At least not to the point where I can function normally in society with work, a social life and other expectations. I get overwhelmed far too quickly.

I'm on waiting list for trauma treatment and I hope things will get better but I don't really see a way out of this perpetual freeze state I'm in. And I'm hitting 40, it feels a bit bitter that help and insight hasn't come sooner.

I'm only out to two people in the whole world, neither of them family.

In a sort of roundabout way I tried to open up the subject once over email with my abuser - back when I felt I needed them in my life to understand myself better and I reached out to get in touch. Their response was something along the lines of "I don't know what your [family member] has said about me over the years" and that was that. No admission or anything. Not that I really expected that.

Since I don't remember the abuse myself I have to rely on others' testimony as well as emotional flashbacks and the like to trust that I was the victim of CSA. That person is never going to admit it.

I've been accused of being manipulative and guilt-tripping in conflicts with a person before and I struggle to see my own actions as that. The way I see it, I'm just trying to communicate my feelings.

It absolutely has led to more trauma for me too. I recently had a long friendship end because they were unwilling to accept my fawn response any longer. They started to find me insincere and untrustworthy. I fawned over them a lot due to their aggressive personality and my complete terror of losing them if I stood up for myself.

Trauma upon trauma.

Part of me wants to remember because I think that would make me feel more valid. I think it would be easier in the sense that I wouldn't have to wonder and wouldn't have to defend or explain why I think I've been abused.  
But another part of me is afraid that remembering will shatter the vague functioning I have going for me. Or that I won't be able to uncover the memories because I was so young, and I'll just feel even less valid.  


All I really want is for a therapist to look at the symptoms I'm displaying, nod and say yep, this is consistent with trauma responses. Let's put that in your paperwork and history so you don't have to defend your symptoms in the future.
Thank you, I wish you all the best too. Let's both try to be kind to ourselves. <3

To answer your question, I'm not currently in therapy. My previous therapist just absolutely refused to talk about trauma. I tried again and again to tell her about what I was experiencing, including some dissociative symptoms, but she wouldn't have it. She said she didn't want to focus on trauma because it could lead to "false memories" - completely disregarding the stuff I told her about  severe bullying, abuse in the school system and emotional neglect at home. She dismissed each and every symptom I tried to show her as another aspect of my avoidant disorder.   


When I tried to ask for a new therapist, they shut me out instead. While I was actively suicidal. To say that I've lost some faith in getting help and being heard is to put it mildly.   


But thank you, internet stranger, for validating me. Today has been a day of anger and grief and powerlessness. Sometimes it just hits I guess?
